Paragraph:
Translation: O King, at that time Arjuna, the son of Pandu, who was seated in his chariot, his flag marked with Hanuman, took up his bow and prepared to shoot his arrows, looking at the sons of Dhrtarastra. O King, Arjuna then spoke to Hrsikesa [Krsna] these words:

Purport (Excerpt): The battle was just about to begin. It is understood from the above statement that the sons of Dhrtarastra were more or less disheartened... The emblem of Hanuman on the flag of Arjuna is another sign of victory because Hanuman cooperated with Lord Rama... Therefore, Arjuna had no cause to fear any enemies whatsoever. And above all, the Lord of the senses, Lord Krsna, was personally present to give him direction... In such auspicious conditions, arranged by the Lord for His eternal devotee, lay the signs of assured victory.
Situation/Problem_Faced: With the opposing army demoralized, Arjuna prepares himself for combat. Seated in an optimal, spiritually supported environment, he raises his weapon, surveys the battlefield, and turns to speak to his guide.
Key_Teaching/Action_Taken: Arjuna assumes a stance of readiness. The presence of powerful psychological and spiritual anchors—Krishna as his guide and the flag of Hanuman (symbolizing past victories of good over evil)—eliminates his fear and sets the stage for optimal performance.
Outcome/Resolution: Arjuna reaches a state of peak readiness and focus, pausing only to communicate with his trusted guide before initiating action.

Spiritual_Psychological_Concept_Indian.Concept: Abhaya (Fearlessness achieved through divine connection and righteous duty)
Svadharma (Readiness to execute one's prescribed duty with full commitment)

Brief_Summary_Spiritual: The verse establishes the perfect conditions for spiritual victory. When a person aligns with divine will (represented by Krishna) and draws inspiration from the heritage of righteousness (Hanuman), fear is entirely eradicated. True readiness comes not just from holding a weapon, but from the auspicious presence of God within one's endeavors.
Brief_Summary_Psychological: Arjuna demonstrates a state of optimal psychological readiness and 'flow' before a major stressor. Surrounded by profound symbols of support and guided by a trusted mentor, he experiences deep psychological safety. This allows him to assess the threat calmly, lift his bow without hesitation, and maintain clear communication with his support system.
